name: dns-doctor
description: Scan, fix, verify and monitor a domain's DNS: email authentication (SPF, DMARC, DKIM) with DMARC monitoring and evidence-based enforcement guidance, plus multi-region propagation, SPF include supply-chain audits, MX, DNS health, blacklists and domain/SSL expiry. Returns deterministic verdicts and copy-paste fix records generated by a validating engine, never a guessed record.

interface.shortDescription: DMARC monitoring plus SPF, DKIM and DMARC diagnostics for any domain. Scan email authentication, find SPF lookup-limit problems, check DKIM and DMARC, generate validated DMARC records, monitor DMARC RUA reports and new senders, and move from p=none to quarantine on a scan's evidence and to reject on report evidence. You publish every record yourself.
interface.longDescription: DMARC monitoring plus SPF, DKIM and DMARC diagnostics for any domain. Scan email authentication, find SPF lookup-limit problems, check DKIM and DMARC, generate validated DMARC records, monitor DMARC RUA reports and new senders, and move from p=none to quarantine on a scan's evidence and to reject on report evidence. You publish every record yourself. Fix records are generated deterministically and RFC-validated, never guessed by AI; SPF is diagnosed, never rewritten. Twenty-two tools: scan a domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, DNS health, blacklists, domain and TLS expiry), read the stored report, build a validated DMARC upgrade or a DMARC record from scratch, validate a pasted DMARC record, count SPF lookups, audit SPF includes, check a DKIM selector, check a record on the domain's own nameservers, check global propagation from six vantage points, check reverse DNS, look up a domain's registration, check which lookalike domains of it resolve, parse a DMARC aggregate report, build the hardening pack for a non-sending domain, hand the owner a monitoring sign-up link, for signed-in operators read the monitoring alert log, the enforcement-readiness verdict and the watched lookalike domains, and for a linked account add a domain, check its verification and read its records. The assistant never signs the user in, never emails on their behalf, and never applies a DNS change: it explains the findings and presents each record for the human to publish.
defaultPrompt: Look up my domain's DNS records and check whether my latest change is live.
Mail from my domain keeps landing in spam. Check its email authentication.
Help me move my domain's DMARC policy to enforcement safely.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.16.0. Email tests now score a message out of 10 to one decimal and estimate, for Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook and Apple, whether it is accepted and whether it reaches the inbox; these are estimates, not promises. Scan reports show each provider's published sender rules against what DNS shows. A domain on Automatic DMARC gets its next DMARC step from the dashboard. If you can't make a DNS change yourself, setup results now include a ready message for your DNS host's support and an email for whoever manages your DNS. Check whether a domain is set up to show its logo in inboxes (BIMI), mailbox by mailbox. See every domain in a linked account with its state and the next step for each. Record lookups now answer done, wait or edit when you check a change you just published, and say where a misplaced edit landed. You publish every DNS change yourself.
